headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Rasa can egress to allowlisted APIs while LangChain4j has no network egress, but the pairwise interaction is otherwise mostly undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection bridge is not documented: LangChain4j shows no I/O surfaces, while Rasa exposes messaging APIs and can ingest external text. The only plausible pathway is manual or application-level handoff from Rasa outputs into LangChain4j prompts, so the blast radius is limited and not default. Uncertainty is low enough to stay at low, not none.
conditions: IF an operator copies Rasa-generated text into a LangChain4j prompt without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared message queue or file bridge is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can traverse it.
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that separates instructions from Rasa text.
Strip markup and control tokens before passing text from B to A.
Add a human review step for any B-to-A handoff.
Disable any shared clipboard or file bridge between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and can send data through allowlisted APIs, while LangChain4j has no network egress. If they share a workspace or operator handoff, sensitive conversation content can flow from B into A's prompts or logs. The pairwise path exists in common deployments, but the evidence does not show uncontrolled third-party exfiltration from A.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same transcript files, B's text and voice-derived content can be read by A.
IF Rasa forwards conversation content to an allowlisted API, that content may leave the local boundary before LangChain4j processes it.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for A and B.
Redact PII from transcripts before any handoff.
Restrict Rasa connectors to the minimum required channels.
Disable logging of raw conversation payloads where possible.
Use a short-lived staging file for any manual transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangChain4j has no declared write or network surfaces, while Rasa explicitly does not support multiple instances and uses a tool-use pattern. That suggests some operational contention is possible, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. Without a shared writable target, conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same conversation store or bot configuration directory, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator launches multiple Rasa instances despite the profile saying it does not support them, state conflicts become more likely.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories to A and B.
Run only one Rasa instance per deployment.
Add file locks around any shared mutable resource.
Avoid concurrent edits to bot configuration files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can act on dialogue inputs and external channels, while LangChain4j can generate content that may be fed into downstream bot logic. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing responses or actions. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Rasa consumes LangChain4j output without validation, hallucinated facts can propagate to users.
IF A-generated text is used as a policy or routing signal inside B, downstream actions may be incorrect.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B uses A's output.
Constrain A to produce structured, schema-validated fields.
Log and review any A-to-B handoff for a short pilot period.
Require confidence thresholds before B acts on A's text.

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and can send data to external messaging APIs, while LangChain4j has no network egress and no declared data classes. This creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if the same customer-support data is processed by both, especially when B forwards content externally. The profiles do not show a specific legal regime, so medium fits the documented gap.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support transcripts are routed through Rasa connectors, external retention policies may apply.
IF LangChain4j is used to process the same transcripts locally, its handling may diverge from B's connector retention rules.
mitigations: Map the data classes each agent handles before deployment.
Avoid sending regulated data through external connectors unless approved.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document the residency of every downstream API used by Rasa.
